title: Business Economics, B.S. (Behrend)
notes: Penn State Erie, The Behrend College is the ONLY Penn State location where this degree exists ('Penn State Behrend is the only location in the Penn State system where you can earn this versatile degree' -- Behrend's own program page) -- there is no University Park equivalent to compare against, so Pattern A/B doesn't apply in the usual sense; this is simply a brand-new plan. New plan code BUSECONBH invented (no existing UP 'Business Economics' major to reuse a code from) and confirmed non-colliding against every existing degree_plans/ major code. Built entirely from Behrend's own 2026-27 Suggested Academic Plan PDF (business-economics-bs_suggestedacademicplantext.pdf), term-by-term. Total credits: 120, matching the bulletin's stated total for every listed row -- PLUS one added MATH 21 course (see below), for a real total of 123. Real prereq fix: ACCTG 211 and SCM 200 (both Second Year Fall, an Entrance-to-Major requirement) each real-require MATH 21 per the shared econ/acctg/scm course catalogs, and the bulletin's own suggested plan never lists MATH 21 anywhere (same hidden-prereq pattern documented across ACCTG-2026, FIN-2026, MKTG-2026, and MGMT-2026's own UP plans) -- added MATH 21 explicitly in First Year Spring (no MATH 3/MATH 4 chain needed like those older UP fixes required, since the current math_catalog.json's own MATH 21 entry now scrapes with an empty prereq_groups list). 'Additional ECON Course' (x4 total: three in Fourth Year Fall, one in Fourth Year Spring) models the bulletin's own 'Economics Electives (Select 12 credits)' category, kept as a generic slot rather than an enumerated pool since the bulletin only names example subareas (Labor Economics, Money and Banking, Experimental and Behavioral Economics, Business Forecasting, Internships, Independent Studies) without a full course-code list -- same honest-generic-slot convention as ECON-2026 UP's own '400-Level ECON elective' slots. 'Supporting Business Course' (x4) and 'Approved Elective' (x6, restricted per the bulletin's own footnote: not a lower-level ENGL 1-6 or MATH 2-41 course, not GHW-designated) are likewise generic, unenumerated per Behrend's own page. Note SCM 200 is listed alone (no 'or STAT 200' alternative) in Second Year Fall -- matching the bulletin's literal suggested-plan text exactly, unlike every other Behrend business major built alongside this one, which do offer the STAT 200 alternative.
